title: Foundation attempt ingress composition
description: Objective: land the authenticated production command edge that selects exactly one Foundation execution-bearing node and invokes Durable Claude attempt dispatch without caller-supplied authority. Deliverable: after daemon command-registry extraction and the shared effect.activate composition land, register the bounded Foundation attempt command through the real HTTP Authenticator/decision registry, derive the one-node claim/activation request from durable graph/session facts, and delegate to task-6cbff010's service. NOT in scope: launcher internals, activation-ledger codec, verification/review, multi-node support, or schema. Current measured gap: only the advisory board work.claim service is registered; pure claimWork/activateEffect/launchClaude have no authenticated daemon production caller, and daemon-store-dependencies.ts is 397 lines.
definitionOfDone: The real daemon HTTP/command registry exposes one bounded Foundation attempt command with exact capability, payload allow-list, family, and stable refusal mapping; authentication runs before payload authority.

The handler derives project/principal/session and current graph/node/claim facts from durable production readers, never accepts caller-selected grant, runtime closure, slot, budget, lease, attempt, effect, or process registration authority.
Exactly one low-risk execution-bearing node delegates to task-6cbff010; zero or more than one refuses with an exact daemon code/layer before claim/activation/provider effects.
Replay uses the store command-decision identity and returns the original dispatch record; conflicting command bytes refuse, with raw event/decision counts and zero duplicate launch invocation.

Focused production-ingress tests use real SqliteEventStore + Authenticator and assert exact code/stage/layer, positive generated case counts, zero residue, and one accepted control; daemon gates and plain-Node provider construction pass.
taskRails: Hard-depend on daemon command-registry extraction task-9cba79a1d75141cf8e78764f4db44fad, the production effect.activate composition task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d, and task-6cbff010.
Do not grow daemon-store-dependencies.ts past 400 or reimplement registry/authentication in a new test helper.
Use public package roots, TDD exact stable reason codes/layers, target <=250 lines and split before 400.
Multi-node/fan-out remains typed UNSUPPORTED with zero authority.
reopenReason: Hard dependencies task-9cba79a1, task-e33747f9, and task-6cbff010 are not DONE. Planning now would invent registry, activation, and dispatch authority; re-open only after all three production consumers are QA-approved.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR — BLOCK NOTE CORRECTED. Your dependency direction is right; the OTHER side of it was wrong, and it made a cycle. Human decision 2026-08-15T17:51Z.

THE CYCLE. This task's block reads: "Hard dependencies task-9cba79a1, task-e33747f9, and task-6cbff010 are not DONE." Meanwhile task-6cbff010's comment-0a2ff71dcbc6 (architect-a42f4965, 08-13) lists THIS task among prerequisites it created for itself. Each was waiting on the other. Neither could ever move, and seven-plus CRITICAL tasks sat behind the pair.

RESOLUTION: task-6cbff010 is UPSTREAM, this task is DOWNSTREAM. Dispatch is the producer; Foundation attempt ingress composes on it. The edge from 6cbff010 to this task was speculative prerequisite-authoring, not a measured composition edge, and has been retired in a comment there. Your block stands as written — do not re-block on the reverse direction.

CURRENT STATE OF YOUR THREE NAMED DEPENDENCIES:
- task-9cba79a1 registry extraction — DONE
- task-e33747f9 effect.activate composition — PLANNING, in flight with architect-797c65f6 (it came out of BLOCKED today; all four of ITS prerequisites landed)
- task-6cbff010 durable Claude attempt dispatch — BLOCKED, but armed: it flips to PLANNING the moment task-e33747f9 reaches DONE and re-measures clean. Every one of its other producers is already DONE.

So the resume order is: task-e33747f9 lands, then task-6cbff010 plans and lands, then this task. Two hops, both moving.

WHEN YOU DO RESUME: re-measure all three at their PUBLIC roots rather than off the status column — DONE is not reachable. Two specifics that will bite: task-df29871b (the activation ledger underneath this chain) was QA-rejected once today for returning the CALLER'S record as durable authority on the replayed path, so probe that path with stored and caller values deliberately DISAGREEING; and task-e33747f9's block forbids manufacturing {...slot,state:'ACTIVE'} in daemon, a prohibition that carries downstream into any composition you build here. If an authority is still missing, re-block with the failing import rather than inventing it.

blockedReason: The task's own hard-dependency condition remains false. Registry extraction task-9cba79a1 is DONE, but task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d is still WORKING (not QA-approved DONE) and its apparent effect.activate changes are/just were foreign in-flight bytes; upstream task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 is BLOCKED awaiting that committed activation path. A committed-HEAD grep for Foundation attempt dispatch/read APIs remains empty, so there is no production service for this ingress to delegate to. Governor comment-55c9ce72 already fixes the direction: e337 -> 6cb -> this task. Planning now would invent the dispatch authority or consume foreign work. Re-promote only after e337 and 6cb are both QA-approved DONE, then probe the registry/public host and stored-dispatch reader with deliberately disagreeing caller/stored replay values before naming symbols. Do not manufacture ACTIVE provider slots or reimplement registry/authentication.
